prompt: In the bench, `subscribed` was logged after `before subscribe`. What does that show?

choices.text: The console reorders messages from the same component
choices.why: The console prints in the order things ran.

choices.text: Making an Observable runs nothing; subscribing does
choices.why: Right. It is lazy.

choices.text: The Observable waited for Angular to finish starting
choices.why: It waited for `subscribe`, which came straight after.

choices.text: `new Observable` is asynchronous, like a Promise
choices.why: `got 1` arrived before `subscribe` returned.

prompt: The bench subscribed twice to one `http.get('/api/planner')`. Counting the store's, how many requests for `/api/planner` did the page make?
Why did two subscriptions to one `http.get(...)` send two requests?

choices.text: `HttpClient` sends every request twice to be safe
choices.why: One subscriber, one request.

choices.text: The proxy duplicates requests to the API
choices.why: The API's log matched the page's network list.

choices.text: It is cold: each subscriber runs the function again
choices.why: Right. For `HttpClient`, the function sends the request.

choices.text: The first subscription failed, and the second retried it
choices.why: Both answered 200.

prompt: Match each with what it gives.

pairs.right: one value or an error, started at once
values over time, from when it is subscribed

right_distractors: a value written once at build time

prompt: `interval(100).pipe(map(n => n * 10), filter(n => n % 20 === 0), take(3))`: which values were logged?

choices.why: `filter` dropped 10.
Right. `take` counted only what `filter` let through.

choices.text: 0, 1 and 2
choices.why: `map` multiplied each by ten first.

choices.text: 0, 20, 40, 60 and on, for ever
choices.why: `take(3)` completed the chain.

prompt: What stopped `interval(100)`, which on its own counts for ever?

choices.text: The component was destroyed
choices.why: The bench stayed on the page.

choices.text: `filter` dropped the values after 40
choices.why: `filter` lets through every multiple of 20.

choices.text: `take(3)`, by completing the chain
choices.why: Right. Completing the end of a chain ends what feeds it.

choices.text: `look` closed the page after a second
choices.why: The chain completed well before; `ticks done` was logged.

prompt: Match each operator with where it earns its place.

pairs.right: a search box, so not every key sends a request
a fallback value instead of a broken screen
a log line in the middle of a chain
not asking the same question twice in a row

right_distractors: turning a signal into a template

prompt: Without `debounceTime`, typing `Jav` sent how many requests from the bench?

choices.text: One, for `Jav`
choices.why: That needed the pause `debounceTime` adds.

choices.text: Three, one per letter
choices.why: The empty query at the start sent one too.

choices.text: Four: the empty query, `J`, `Ja` and `Jav`
choices.why: Right. One per value the query had.

choices.text: None until the box lost focus
choices.why: Each `input` event set the signal at once.

prompt: What does `debounceTime(300)` do with the values of the query?

choices.text: It passes one on only after 300 ms with no newer one
choices.why: Right. A burst of keys becomes one value.

choices.text: It delays every value by 300 ms and passes all of them
choices.why: That is `delay`; `debounceTime` drops the ones overtaken.

choices.text: It cancels any request slower than 300 ms
choices.why: It acts on the values before any request exists.

choices.text: It lets one value through every 300 ms
choices.why: That is closer to `throttleTime`.

prompt: Over a slow network, the answer for `Ja` arrives after the answer for `Jav`. Which operator keeps the screen right?

choices.text: `mergeMap`, which keeps every answer
choices.why: It would show `Ja`'s results under a box that says `Jav`.

choices.text: `concatMap`, which keeps them in order
choices.why: It would wait for every old answer, and show each in turn.

choices.text: `switchMap`, which cancels
choices.why: Right. An old answer cannot land, because it was never kept.

choices.text: `exhaustMap`, which ignores new values while busy
choices.why: It would drop `Jav` and show `Ja`.

prompt: Match each operator with what it does when a new value arrives while a request is still out.

pairs.right: cancels the old request, starts the new one
starts the new one and keeps both
waits for the old one, then starts
ignores the new value until done

right_distractors: sends both values in one request

choices.text: Nothing; call `unsubscribe` in `ngOnDestroy`
choices.why: It does it for you.

choices.text: It unsubscribes when its component or service is destroyed
choices.why: Right. That is why it needs an injection context.

choices.text: It unsubscribes after the first value
choices.why: It keeps the latest value as long as it lives.

choices.text: It never subscribes until the template reads it
choices.why: It subscribes at once.

prompt: A template writes `{{ left$ | async }}` twice. What happens?

choices.text: One subscription, shared by both
choices.why: Each pipe subscribes on its own.

choices.text: A build error: one Observable, one `async`
choices.why: It compiles.

choices.text: The second shows nothing until the first completes
choices.why: Both show the value when their request answers.

choices.text: Two subscriptions, and since it is cold, two requests
choices.why: Right. `@if (left$ | async; as left)` subscribes once.

prompt: Inside a constructor, `.pipe(___())` completes a subscription when the component is destroyed.
The store retries a failed `PATCH` only when `transient(error)` is true. Why not on a 400?

choices.text: A 400 means the API is restarting
choices.why: A 400 is the API refusing the body.

choices.text: It fails the same way each time
choices.why: Right. Retrying a refusal is noise.

choices.text: `retry` cannot see the status code
choices.why: The `delay` function receives the error, status and all.

choices.text: A 400 is retried by the browser on its own
choices.why: The browser retries nothing on a 400.

prompt: In the retry run, the first `PATCH` got a 500. What happened next?

choices.text: The box unticked and the message appeared
choices.why: That is what happens once the retries run out.

choices.text: The page reloaded the planner from the API
choices.why: Only the `PATCH` was sent again.

choices.text: It was sent again two seconds later, and saved
choices.why: Right. The box stayed ticked.

choices.text: Nothing: `retry` waits for the next tick
choices.why: It sent the same request again on its own.

prompt: Why will lesson 14's `POST` that adds a session not retry?

choices.text: A `POST` cannot be piped through `retry`
choices.why: Any Observable can.

choices.text: The API refuses a second `POST` from the same page
choices.why: It accepts every valid one.

choices.text: Adding a session never fails
choices.why: It fails on a bad field, and with the API down.

choices.text: A lost answer would mean a second session
choices.why: Right. Only what is safe twice is retried.

prompt: Which of these call for RxJS rather than a signal? Choose every one.

choices.text: Waiting for a pause in typing
choices.why: Right. `debounceTime`.

choices.text: Keeping only the newest of overlapping requests
choices.why: Right. `switchMap`.

choices.text: Holding whether a panel is open
choices.why: A `signal` holds that.

choices.text: The week's total, worked out from the sessions
choices.why: A `computed` works it out.

choices.text: Trying a request again two seconds later
choices.why: Right. `retry` with a `delay`.

prompt: Old code keeps the selected course in a `BehaviorSubject` and every template reads it with `| async`. You are changing one screen. What does the lesson suggest?

choices.text: Rewrite every screen to signals first
choices.why: Nothing obliges a rewrite of code that works.

choices.text: Leave it, since signals and Observables cannot meet
choices.why: `toSignal` and `toObservable` exist to make them meet.

choices.text: Read it with `toSignal` in the screen you change
choices.why: Right. The two kinds meet at the edge of what you touched.

choices.text: Subscribe to it in the constructor, with no cleanup
choices.why: That is the leak `toSignal` avoids.
